description: I am a first year biomedical student. I dont know much about coding or anything. Just here for my first hackathon. If you can help me and contribute, I would be happy to accept you to the team
summary:
Vitals Deck is an offline health self-check for astronauts on long missions. Crew log a two-minute daily check-in covering vitals, sleep, mood, exercise, cabin CO₂ and radiation. The app then flags problems against fixed limits, personal baselines, trends and patterns, shows a clickable body map, and gives clear next steps.
Also even if they want to send a message to earth it would take 3-22 minutes to arrive and another 22 minutes to receive a response. that's why its offline
details:
Here are the details about your project, structured around the questions you asked:

  • What it does and how it works

    • It is an instrument-panel dashboard and crew health self-assessment tool designed for spaceflight environments (such as a low Earth orbit station, lunar transit, or Mars transit).
    • It allows crew members to log a daily check-in of vital physiological and psychological indicators (including resting heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, blood oxygen, glucose, sleep, mood, exercise minutes, cabin CO₂, and radiation dose).
    • It evaluates these entries against absolute safety limits, personal baselines established over the first 7 check-ins, multi-day trends, and known clinical symptom combinations to flag potential health risks.
    • It provides actionable self-care steps or flags when to contact the crew medical officer or flight surgeon, alongside a generated report summary that can be copied.
    • Empowers crew members to monitor health proactively in isolated environments without requiring live telemetry links.
    • Accounts for communication delays on deep space missions (such as Mars transit) by providing immediate, local triage guidance.
    • Tracks longitudinal trends rather than just isolated noise, catching multi-day drifts in sleep, exercise, or mood.
    • Mitigates prominent human spaceflight hazards identified by NASA's Human Research Program—such as cardiovascular deconditioning, behavioral strain, sleep disruption, and reduced musculoskeletal fitness.
    • Enhances crew autonomy and safety during long-duration exploration missions.
    • Built as a complete, offline-first web application using standard front-end web technologies (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript wrapped in a single file).
    • Leverages local storage to keep user readings securely and privately within the browser.
    • Designed to mirror manual data logging procedures used with actual spacecraft medical devices.
    • Translates complex aerospace medical frameworks and NASA Human Research Program risk lists into an intuitive, gamified instrument-panel aesthetic with interactive body maps and real-time visual status indicators.
    • Features adaptive feedback that tracks custom baselines and multi-symptom patterns (like headache paired with high cabin CO₂ or short sleep paired with low mood) rather than isolated thresholds.
    • Operational Realism: Factoring in communication light-speed delays for deep space exploration versus low Earth orbit.
    • Privacy & Reliability: Ensuring the app works entirely offline inside a browser without relying on external servers or cloud databases.
    • Psychological Safety: Rewarding consistency (streaks and logging) rather than penalizing bad health numbers, keeping the tool supportive and honest.
